title: A proper morphism carries rationally equivalent cycles to rationally equivalent cycles
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The lemma is the functoriality statement that a proper morphism preserves rational equivalence, p_* alpha rationally equivalent to p_* beta whenever alpha and beta are (statement lines 3216-3223, tag 02S2). Although the statement looks formal, the proof is a real reduction: it distributes the pushforward over the locally finite family, reduces to a single integral W and its image W', and then distinguishes three dimension cases, the delicate one being dim_delta(W') = k where one must observe that the fibre over the generic point of W' is a proper integral curve over a field, that its closed points correspond to the integral subschemes through which the divisor passes, and that the multiplicity of the image class equals the multiplicity of [Spec(K)] in the pushforward of the principal divisor, which vanishes. The identification of the multiplicities is the substance, so the claim is H2.
